performance.Description:
The Revolutionists
By Lauren Gunderson
Directed by Meg Peart

October 22, 23, 24, 25, 29, 30 & 31 at 7:30 PM
November 1 at 2:00 PM
Boathouse Theatre at Valhalla Tahoe
Tickets: $25

Four women. One revolution. And a story worth losing your head over.

Set during the French Revolution’s Reign of Terror, The Revolutionists is a bold, fast-paced comedy about four remarkable women trying to change the world while trying not to lose their heads.

Playwright Olympe de Gouges is desperately searching for something meaningful to write when her world is interrupted by three extraordinary women: assassin Charlotte Corday, Haitian revolutionary Marianne Angelle, and former Queen of France Marie Antoinette. Together, they wrestle with art, activism, friendship, legacy, and what it means to stand up for something when everything is on the line.

Funny, fierce, irreverent, and unexpectedly moving, Lauren Gunderson’s The Revolutionists takes a wildly theatrical look at the French Revolution through the stories of women too often left out of the history books.

The Cast
Stephanie Grigsby as Olympe de Gouges
Joanie San Agustin as Charlotte Corday
Ginger Nicolay Davis as Marie Antoinette
Courtney Cobble as Marianne Angelle

Directed by Meg Peart

An Immersive Night at the Boathouse
For this production, the experience begins before the first line is spoken. The Boathouse Theatre will be transformed to bring audiences into the world of revolutionary France, creating an intimate and immersive evening on the shores of Lake Tahoe.

Come early, grab a drink, step into the revolution, and prepare for a night of theatre that is equal parts hilarious, poignant, rebellious, and wonderfully theatrical.

Halloween at The Revolutionists — October 31
Our Halloween performance gets a revolutionary twist!

Costumes are encouraged—but completely optional—for our October 31 performance. Come dressed for the French Revolution, channel your favorite historical or literary figure, or simply arrive ready for a night at the theatre.

The revolution is coming to the Boathouse. Try not to lose your head.

performance.Description:
Guilty Christmas
Written By David Hamilton and Mark D. Williams

Directed by David Hamilton

November 18 - 22 at 7:30 PM
Boathouse Theatre at Valhalla Tahoe
Tickets: $25 - General Admission | $15 Children 12 and under

The Perfect Way to get into the Christmas Spirit

The characters from the long-running Guilty Pleasures (2002–2012) are returning for a winter show
filled with sketches, songs and fast-paced comedy, written specifically for Tahoe audiences—locals
and visitors alike.

It’s been a while since this group of characters served their community service together, but
somehow, they’ve all managed to come together again. They’re older—though perhaps not much
wiser—and this time they’re ready to celebrate the winter, Tahoe-style.

Written by Dave Hamilton and Mark D. Williams, Guilty Christmas features songs about winter
driving, surviving the big snowstorm and all the other joys and challenges of a Tahoe winter. The
show also brings back a couple of favorite songs from the original Guilty Pleasures productions.
And, of course, there’s the popular giant finale, featuring practically every Christmas carol you’ve ever
heard.

The entire Guilty Christmas cast is returning, with Tom Callahan, Anita Kelley, Sharon Kerrigan, Kurt
Munger, Joanie San Agustin, Chris Taylor, Pam Taylor, Liz Tonkinson and Jeff Whitt reprising their
roles.

If you saw Guilty Christmas a couple of years ago, there will be plenty of new material to enjoy. And if
you remember Guilty Pleasures, then you already know just what you’re in for. If this is all new to you,
even better—just sit back, laugh and enjoy the ride with everyone else.

Come celebrate Christmas and laugh at all the quirks, frustrations and absurdities of living in Tahoe
during the winter. Because nothing says “Happy Holidays” quite like snow, traffic, giant snowbanks
and questionable driving decisions.

Performances November 18-22, 7:30pm
Tickets are $25 general, $15 children 12 and under
All performances are at the Valhalla Boathouse Theatre
